sections.content: Describing an ideal home requires more than listing rooms and adjectives. A B1 speaker can combine relative clauses, comparisons, reasons and hypothetical language to explain what makes a home suitable. This creates connected evaluation rather than a list of isolated features.

items.spanish: La casa que elegiría tendría un jardín, aunque sería más cara que un piso.
items.english: The house I would choose would have a garden, although it would be more expensive than a flat.

items.spanish: Prefiero una vivienda que sea funcional porque necesito espacio para trabajar.
items.english: I prefer a home that is functional because I need space to work.

items.spanish: El lugar sería acogedor y tendría suficiente privacidad para que pudiéramos convivir cómodamente.
items.english: The place would be welcoming and have enough privacy so that we could live together comfortably.

items.spanish: Aunque no sería muy grande, tendría un entorno tranquilo y estaría bien comunicado.
items.english: Although it would not be very large, it would have quiet surroundings and be well connected.

sections.content: A useful B1 description can move from feature to evaluation to reason: what the home is like, how it compares with alternatives, and why it would suit the people living there.
